summary: Opaque native addon with browser-credential-lookup, host-reconnaissance, and HTTP/TLS-client capabilities shipped as sole entry point
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB Linux x64 Rust native addon (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) as its `main` entry point, with a one-line README and no repository, author, homepage, or description in `package.json`. String analysis of the binary reveals a combined capability set characteristic of a credential stealer: browser login database lookup markers (`Found login for`, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER`), host reconnaissance strings (`network_adapters`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `bogomips per cpu`, `CPU implementer`, `gethostname`, `getifaddrs`), a full TLS HTTP client (ureq/rustls), zip/zstd compression support, and process spawn primitives (`posix_spawnp`, `execvp`). The package uses a generic non-scoped name and a version string (`3.1.40-browser-release-151-359-1784544869`) whose numeric suffix decodes to a future-dated Unix timestamp. Requiring this package causes the opaque native code to load and execute in-process on the installer's machine; the capability fingerprint (browser login + SQLite auth string handling + host recon + outbound TLS + archive packaging + subprocess spawn) matches the credential-stealer / exfiltration shape, though the specific destination could not be recovered from strings alone.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
